target_customer: Bloggers and site owners who wanted to run contests and giveaways
problem: Running a contest on a website meant handling entries, rules, winners and dates by hand. ContestMachine offered an embeddable widget that handled submissions, requirements, timing and winner contact.
business_model: Hosted contest widget service, pricing not stated in sources found

founders.name: Savraj Singh
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says YC S07 and W09, currently at Bubble Goods

founders.name: Kalid Azad
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page

founders.name: Lee Linden
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page

exit.reason: YC page says no longer in business; cause not public

technical_complexity.rationale: An embeddable widget with entry handling and winner selection, standard web work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Contest forms could be built with generic form tools and had little switching cost.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent move found. The company closed.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in September 2008 pitched it as a product giveaway widget for bloggers, but no demand or usage figures were found.

branding.domain_note: contestmachine.com is parked on a GoDaddy for sale page
branding.community_and_virality: A TechCrunch post of 2008-09-06 and a The Next Web post of 2008-09-07 covered the launch.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that says what it does but is generic, with two launch posts and no further brand signal.

outcome_analysis: ContestMachine came out of Crystalroot, which the YC directory dates to Summer 2007, and launched publicly in September 2008 per TechCrunch. The company is no longer in business according to its YC page. No post mortem or press about the closing was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are asserted. A niche widget with low switching cost and unclear willingness to pay may have struggled, but no source says so.
notes: Funding conflict: CB Insights reports about $20K from YC; Dealroom lists a $125k seed (the same value Dealroom shows for Wundrbar, so possibly a template). The $20K is recorded and rests on a single database with no date. Batch conflict: YC says Summer 2007; Seedtable says S08. The TechCrunch and Next Web launch posts name no competitors, so the list is empty. Founder list comes from the YC page; backgrounds not found. Dead-site note: contestmachine.com is parked for sale.
